reviews.conclusion: After the completed End fight, the player enters the exit portal. The view is black and then shows the dirt transition background from proxy 4.25 through 14.75 s before returning to the overworld. The 10.5-11 s sampled transition bounds contain the 10.767 s deficit. This is post-completion transition behavior, not a same-world gameplay edit indication. Exact native-frame GUI-clock accounting remains unverified.

Nether portal travel into a stronghold and then End entry include loading and multiple menu sessions: proxy 8-10, 12.75-13, 14, 21.5-22.5 and 24.5 s. Their combined sampled duration bounds are 3.25-5.75 s, compatible with the 4.633 s deficit. Inventory screens are not counted as pauses; no exact native-frame closure is asserted.

An eye measurement includes settings at proxy 6.5-6.75 s and game/settings menus at 11-13.25 s. Their 2.5-3.5 s aggregate sampled duration is compatible with the 3.225 s deficit. A rearranged narrow capture at 9-10.75 s has unknown pause state, so exact accounting remains unresolved.

Nether exit reaches a loading frame at proxy 3.75 s, then a game menu holds from 4-6.75 s before overworld traversal resumes. Its 2.75-3.25 s sampled bounds contain the 2.875 s deficit. The loading transition is recorded separately, and native-frame exact closure is unverified.
A pause/options/video-settings sequence in the fortress lasts 1.25-1.75 s, compatible with -1.4667 s. It is followed by continued combat; no cut is established from this sampled proxy.

coverage.interpretation: Evidence-span interpolation between events in resolved, nonambiguous segments; not proof of continuity throughout those spans or the whole video. Matching heart modes are inference alternatives, not observed heart states.
